title: TS SDK: unified pull-stream API to reconcile AsyncIterator and Web Streams
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: design and implement a small, ergonomic pull-based surface in the TypeScript SDK that makes it straightforward for application developers to consume Redwood streaming responses as either AsyncIterator (for Node/Deno) or ReadableStream/Web Streams (for browsers and frameworks), while preserving cancellation, retry hooks, backpressure signals, and resume-on-reconnect semantics.

Background: we have multiple internal patterns and several community requests for better interop between AsyncIterator consumer code, for-await-of patterns, and browser Web Streams (pipeTo/pipeThrough/ReadableStream). Existing guidance fragments are spread across playbooks and PRs; this ticket consolidates a production API, examples, and conformance tests.

Non-goals: implementing a complete polyfill for non-standard runtimes (e.g., Bun-specific shims) beyond minimal conditional exports; supporting legacy callback APIs; changing the runtime wire format or server-side streaming contract in this scope.

Key constraints and trade-offs: keep the public surface tiny (<=3 entrypoints), prefer zero-dependency runtime detection, ensure type-safe cancellation token patterns, and avoid introducing heavy runtime adapters that increase bundle size for browser consumers. Decisions should favor predictable behavior for token-level billing and transformation hooks (retries, partial results).
acceptance_criteria: Expose a small API: streamToAsyncIterator(streamResponse) and streamToReadable(streamResponse, opts) with clear typings
Cancellation should propagate to the underlying request and free KV cache/compute resources within 50ms in Node sims
Backpressure semantics: async iterator consumers should be able to pause/resume without token duplication; browser ReadableStream pipeTo should apply backpressure to the runtime queue
Comprehensive examples: Node for-await-of example, browser pipeTo example, and a dual consumer (server + browser) migration doc
Integration tests covering: cancellation, mid-stream retry with idempotent responses, error boundaries, and resume after transient network disconnect in a mocked environment
Documentation in SDK reference and a short migration guide in docs repo
tasks: Draft API surface and public TS types
Prototype a minimal adapter that converts SDK fetch/response to AsyncIterator
Prototype ReadableStream wrapper that uses the same pull-based queue and mirrors cancellation
Add unit tests for cancellation and error propagation
Add e2e tests simulating slow consumer/backpressure
Write examples and docs (Node, Browser, Deno) and a migration guide
Submit PR to main repo and get engineering + DX review
Measure bundle delta for browser entrypoints and add tree-shaking notes

comments: 2025-01-10 - Ava Chen: Created ticket after sync with DX and runtime teams. Collected initial user stories from support and solutions engineering. Asked for a small public surface and strong examples.

2025-01-12 - Diego Martinez: Spike complete: two approaches prototyped: (A) adapter that exposes AsyncIterator by consuming a lower-level readable stream API; (B) ReadableStream wrapper that pulls from a unified internal queue. Approach B is slightly more complex but yields smaller bundles for browser consumers. Attached prototype PR link.

2025-01-13 - Maya Patel (DX): Reviewed prototypes. Preference for API names that play nicely with for-await-of and the Streams API. Suggest exposing explicit cancel(token) method and a simple helper to convert to Node Streams (legacy interop).

2025-01-14 - Diego Martinez: Implemented cancellation token and added early teardown hook to the runtime request layer. Found a race where mid-stream retry could double-emit a token unless we checkpoint the last-emitted cursor; added unit test that reproduces the issue.

2025-01-16 - Security (Jonah Kim): Quick review: no new persistent credentials, but flagged that ReadableStream piping to third-party transforms must not leak raw request IDs in thrown errors. Added a small scrub step for error messages.

2025-01-18 - Diego Martinez: Added browser example demonstrating pipeTo with a transform stream and a note about MIME sniffing in Safari. Measuring bundle delta: +1.3KB gzipped for optional adapter path; acceptable.

2025-01-20 - Ava Chen: Requesting design + DX review before merging. Please add a short migration note for customers using existing internal helpers to avoid surprise behavioral changes on cancel/abort.
